## Context
A completion close always dispatches the billable verifier after deterministic guards, even when the ticket already carries a cryptographically certified `completion-verifier` PASS bound to the exact immutable commit being closed. The existing signature verifier can authenticate the stored completion op-cert, but the close seam never consults it. A runtime probe created a certified same-ref completion record on an in-progress bug, then closed at that exact SHA: the provider spy was called once.

The earlier standalone `verify-completion` command returns a signable result but does not persist an attestation. Changing that command into a mutating producer is out of scope; reuse applies only when a genuine ticket-contained completion attestation already exists (for example, from the trusted op-cert producer). The closed Locust task concerns bounded retry of insufficiency-only FAILs and is not a duplicate.

## Proven root cause
`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py::_completion_precheck` unconditionally calls `close_autoresume.verify_with_auto_resume` after its deterministic guards. `verify_with_auto_resume` immediately invokes `llm.verify_completion`; neither seam checks the ticket's existing `completion-verifier` attestation. The required verifier, SHA pin, and material fingerprint are already available from the signature and plan-material infrastructure.

## Repair plan
- Add a fail-safe reuse check at the close auto-resume seam before provider dispatch.
- Resolve the close target ref once and require the stored completion op-cert to certify cryptographically.
- Require an authenticated `completion-verifier: PASS` manifest.
- Require the authenticated `verified-at-sha` to equal the resolved close target SHA.
- Require the authenticated material fingerprint to equal the ticket's current material fingerprint.
- Reject attestations invalidated by a later reopen.
- Return a close-compatible reused PASS result so the normal close, durable verdict, and post-close signing path remain unchanged.
- Fall through to the existing verifier for every absent, malformed, unverifiable, stale, differently pinned, or otherwise ineligible record.

## Test contract card
- authoritative_contract: operator-approved same-ref attested-PASS reuse requirement on this ticket.
- trigger_preconditions: ticket is in progress; completion gate enabled; a completion-verifier op-cert is already stored; explicit --ref resolves to the op-cert SHA.
- production_path: transition -> close precheck -> close autoresume/reuse seam -> locked close -> completion signing.
- observable_postcondition: provider call count is zero and the ticket closes signed.
- negative_controls: different SHA, invalid signature, missing pin, stale material, and pre-reopen attestation each call the provider exactly once.
- test_tier: lifecycle integration over an ephemeral git repo and real ticket store, with only the provider replaced by a spy.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A close at the exact SHA of a valid stored completion PASS makes zero completion-provider calls.
- [x] A reused PASS still produces a signed closed ticket.
- [x] A reused PASS leaves durable completion evidence for the closed ticket.
- [x] A changed resolved ref forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] A cryptographically invalid completion record forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] A non-PASS or wrong-kind record forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] An attestation without an authenticated SHA pin forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] An attestation without an authenticated material fingerprint forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] A material fingerprint mismatch forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] An attestation invalidated by a later reopen forces a fresh completion verification.
- [x] Explicit CLI `--ref` reaches the reuse decision through the normal lifecycle path.
- [x] Focused tests pass.
- [x] `make lint` passes.
- [x] `make typecheck` passes.
